reason.description: Optional one-line reason the suggestion is no longer needed, e.g. "fixed in this session" or "superseded by task_ab12cd34".

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

title.description: Under 60 chars. Imperative action phrase (start with a verb), e.g. "Fix stale README badge", "Remove dead config option". Shown as the chip label and the spawned session title.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tldr.description: One or two plain-English sentences shown on the suggestion card under the title. Lead with why you are suggesting this now — name what you noticed in this session — then say what the new session will do. Keep it readable: no file paths or code.

cwd.description: Optional. Absolute path to a different project root than the current session's — a path on the host this session runs on. The spawned session gets a fresh worktree under this path. Defaults to the current project — only set this when the work clearly belongs in another repo on that host.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

1	"""Best-of-K selection as a point of the KL slice: tie rules, containment, the DV bound.
2	
3	Companion to ``paper/selection_law_kl_containment.md`` and to section 1 of
4	the crosswalk note.  Nothing here calls a model or runs a loop; every law is
5	a finite table of rationals, and the only floats are logarithms, square roots
6	and one Gaussian quadrature, compared under stated tolerances.
7	
8	Setting.  A finite record space ``Omega`` with base law ``p0`` and a score
9	``S``.  ``K`` candidates are drawn i.i.d. from ``p0`` and the best-scoring one
10	is kept; ties are broken by the first index attaining the maximum or
11	uniformly among those attaining it.  Under the Spiral null (axiom A5)
12	``Omega = {0,1}^n``, ``p0 = Bern(p)^n``, ``S = count / n``, and the selection
13	gap ``gamma(n, K, p) = E[max_k S_k] - p`` of ``selection_inflation`` is the
14	mean of ``S - p`` under the selected record's law.
15	
16	1. Tie rules (Theorem A).  Under either rule the selected record has law
17	   ``pi_K(w) = p0(w) P(max = S(w)) / P0(S = S(w))``: ``p0`` conditioned on the
18	   score, mixed over the law of the maximum.  Hence ``KL(pi_K || p0)`` equals
19	   the KL of the law of the maximum of ``K`` scores against the law of one.
20	2. Containment (Theorem B).  ``KL(pi_K || p0) <= ln K - (K-1)/K`` for every
21	   finite ``p0``, score and ``K``, strictly for ``K >= 2``: continuous jitter
22	   removes ties, the jittered selection has KL exactly ``ln K - (K-1)/K``, and
23	   dropping the jitter is a common deterministic map (Jensen on ``x ln x``).
24	3. The DV bound (Theorem C).  With the Kearns-Saul proxy ``v(p)`` of a
25	   Bernoulli, ``gamma(n,K,p) <= sqrt(2 v(p) KL(pi_K||p0) / n)
26	   <= sqrt(2 v(p) (ln K - (K-1)/K) / n)``.
27	4. Uniformity (Question D).  ``gamma / (sigma_n sqrt(2 lambda_K))`` tends to
28	   0 as ``K`` grows at fixed ``n`` and to ``c_K = E[max of K standard
29	   normals] / sqrt(2 lambda_K) < 1`` as ``n`` grows at ``p = 1/2``; ``c_K -> 1``,
30	   so the supremum of the ratio is 1 and is not attained.  At ``n = 1`` the
31	   gap equals the KL-ball supremum exactly.
32	5. Monotone approach (D.5, version 0.2).  With ``a_n(K) = sqrt(n) gamma(n, K, 1/2)``
33	   (so ``r(n, K, 1/2) = 2 a_n(K) / sqrt(2 lambda_K)``), ``a_n(2)^2 = n C(2n,n)^2 /
34	   (4 * 16^n)`` by de Moivre's mean absolute deviation, ``a_{n+1}(2)^2 / a_n(2)^2 =
35	   1 + 1/(4n(n+1))``, and ``a_n(3) = (3/2) a_n(2)`` by the order-statistic
36	   recurrence; both rise strictly to ``E[max]/2``, so ``sup_n r = c_K`` for
37	   ``K = 2, 3``.  For ``K = 4, 5, 10, 20`` (``n <= 200``), ``K = 2..30, 40, 50, 100``
38	   (``n <= 100``) and ``K = 1000`` (``n <= 40``) the increase is verified exactly on ``a_n^2``; the general
39	   case reduces to a second-order inequality (``rho_n + rho_n^2/(4n) >= 1``)
40	   that is not proved, and the convex order ``Z_n <=_cx Z_{n+1}`` of
41	   standardized counts, which would have settled it, fails at every step.
42	"""
43	
44	from __future__ import annotations
45	
46	from fractions import Fraction as Q
47	from functools import lru_cache
48	from itertools import product
49	from math import comb, erfc, exp, log, pi, sqrt
50	
51	import numpy as np
52	
53	from spiral_ln.evaluation_game_feedback import selection_inflation
54	
55	TIE_RULES = ("first_index", "uniform")
56	PROXIES = ("kearns_saul", "hoeffding")
57	LOG_TOLERANCE = 1e-12
58	SUPREMUM_TOLERANCE = 1e-9
59	QUADRATURE_TOLERANCE = 1e-9
60	GRID_ITEMS = (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 64)
61	GRID_CANDIDATES = (2, 3, 5, 10, 20)
62	GRID_P = (Q(1, 4), Q(1, 2), Q(3, 4))
63	GAUSSIAN_CANDIDATES = (2, 3, 5, 10, 100, 1000, 10000)
64	MONOTONE_ITEMS = 200
65	MONOTONE_CANDIDATES = (3, 4, 5, 10, 20)
66	SWEEP_ITEMS = 100
67	SWEEP_CANDIDATES = tuple(range(2, 31)) + (40, 50, 100)
68	LARGE_CANDIDATES, LARGE_ITEMS = 1000, 40
69	STOP_LOSS_MARGIN = 1e-6
70	
71	
72	# --- argument checks ------------------------------------------------------------
73	
74	def _law(law: dict, name: str) -> dict:
75	    if not isinstance(law, dict) or not law:
76	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a non-empty dict of rational masses")
77	    exact = {}
78	    for key, mass in law.items():
79	        if isinstance(mass, float):
80	            raise ValueError(f"{name} must use exact rationals, not floats")
81	        exact[key] = Q(mass)
82	    if any(mass < 0 for mass in exact.values()) or sum(exact.values()) != 1:
83	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be non-negative and sum to one")
84	    return exact
85	
86	
87	def _candidates(candidates: int) -> None:
88	    if type(candidates) is not int or candidates < 1:
89	        raise ValueError("candidates must be a positive integer")
90	
91	
92	def _scores(p0: dict, score: dict) -> dict:
93	    if not isinstance(score, dict) or set(score) != set(p0):
94	        raise ValueError("score must be defined on exactly the records of p0")
95	    if any(isinstance(value, float) for value in score.values()):
96	        raise ValueError("scores must be exact (int or Fraction)")
97	    return {record: Q(value) for record, value in score.items()}
98	
99	
100	def _items(items: int) -> None:
101	    if type(items) is not int or items < 1:
102	        raise ValueError("items must be a positive integer")
103	
104	
105	def _interior_probability(p) -> Q:
106	    if isinstance(p, float):
107	        raise ValueError("p must be an exact rational")
108	    p = Q(p)
109	    if not 0 < p < 1:
110	        raise ValueError("p must lie strictly inside (0, 1)")
111	    return p
112	
113	
114	# --- Theorem A: the selected record's law under a tie rule ----------------------
115	
116	def score_law(p0: dict, score: dict) -> dict[Q, Q]:
117	    """Push-forward of ``p0`` under the score: ``q(s) = P0(S = s)``."""
118	
119	    p0 = _law(p0, "p0")
120	    score = _scores(p0, score)
121	    q: dict[Q, Q] = {}
122	    for record, mass in p0.items():
123	        q[score[record]] = q.get(score[record], Q(0)) + mass
124	    return q
125	
126	
127	def score_cdf(q: dict[Q, Q]) -> dict[Q, tuple[Q, Q]]:
128	    """``s -> (F(s-), F(s))`` for every atom ``s`` of the score law ``q``."""
129	
130	    q = _law(q, "score law")
131	    running, table = Q(0), {}
132	    for s in sorted(q):
133	        table[s] = (running, running + q[s])
134	        running += q[s]
135	    return table
136	
137	
138	def max_law(q: dict[Q, Q], candidates: int) -> dict[Q, Q]:
139	    """Law of the maximum of ``candidates`` i.i.d. scores: ``P(max = s) = F(s)^K - F(s-)^K``."""
140	
141	    _candidates(candidates)
142	    return {s: upto**candidates - below**candidates for s, (below, upto) in score_cdf(q).items()}
143	
144	
145	def first_index_weight(below: Q, upto: Q, candidates: int) -> Q:
146	    """``sum_{k=1}^K F(s-)^{k-1} F(s)^{K-k}``: the first-index rule's multiplier of ``p0(w)``.
147	
148	    Candidate ``k`` is kept with record ``w`` iff it is ``w``, every earlier
149	    candidate scores strictly below ``S(w)`` and every later one at most ``S(w)``.
150	    """
151	
152	    return sum((below**(k - 1) * upto**(candidates - k) for k in range(1, candidates + 1)), Q(0))
153	
154	
155	def uniform_weight(below: Q, upto: Q, candidates: int) -> Q:
156	    """``sum_{j=0}^{K-1} C(K, j+1) q^j F(s-)^{K-1-j}``: the uniform rule's multiplier of ``p0(w)``.
157	
158	    By exchangeability the kept record is ``w`` with probability ``K`` times
159	    the chance that candidate 1 is ``w``, the others score at most ``S(w)``,
160	    and candidate 1 wins the uniform draw among the ``1 + N'`` candidates at
161	    the top, ``N' ~ Bin(K-1, q)`` on that event; ``K C(K-1, j) / (j+1) = C(K, j+1)``.
162	    """
163	
164	    q = upto - below
165	    return sum((comb(candidates, j + 1) * q**j * below**(candidates - 1 - j) for j in range(candidates)), Q(0))
166	
167	
168	def selected_record_law(p0: dict, score: dict, candidates: int, rule: str = "uniform") -> dict:
169	    """Exact law of the record kept by best-of-``candidates`` selection under ``rule``."""
170	
171	    if rule not in TIE_RULES:
172	        raise ValueError("unknown tie rule")
173	    _candidates(candidates)
174	    p0 = _law(p0, "p0")
175	    score = _scores(p0, score)
176	    cdf = score_cdf(score_law(p0, score))
177	    weight = first_index_weight if rule == "first_index" else uniform_weight
178	    return {record: mass * weight(*cdf[score[record]], candidates) for record, mass in p0.items()}
179	
180	
181	def conditioned_on_max_law(p0: dict, score: dict, candidates: int) -> dict:
182	    """``p0(w) P(max = S(w)) / P0(S = S(w))``: ``p0`` conditioned on the score, mixed over the maximum."""
183	
184	    _candidates(candidates)
185	    p0 = _law(p0, "p0")
186	    score = _scores(p0, score)
187	    q = score_law(p0, score)
188	    m = max_law(q, candidates)
189	    return {record: (mass * m[score[record]] / q[score[record]] if mass else Q(0))
190	            for record, mass in p0.items()}
191	
192	
193	def brute_force_selected_law(p0: dict, score: dict, candidates: int, rule: str = "uniform") -> dict:
194	    """Enumerate every ``candidates``-tuple of records and apply the tie rule literally."""
195	
196	    if rule not in TIE_RULES:
197	        raise ValueError("unknown tie rule")
198	    _candidates(candidates)
199	    p0 = _law(p0, "p0")
200	    score = _scores(p0, score)
201	    support = [record for record, mass in p0.items() if mass > 0]
202	    law = {record: Q(0) for record in p0}
203	    for draw in product(support, repeat=candidates):
204	        weight = Q(1)
205	        for record in draw:
206	            weight *= p0[record]
207	        top = max(score[record] for record in draw)
208	        attaining = [k for k, record in enumerate(draw) if score[record] == top]
209	        if rule == "first_index":
210	            law[draw[attaining[0]]] += weight
211	        else:
212	            for k in attaining:
213	                law[draw[k]] += weight / len(attaining)
214	    return law
215	
216	
217	# --- divergences -----------------------------------------------------------------
218	
219	def kl_divergence(pi: dict, p0: dict) -> float:
220	    """``KL(pi || p0)`` in nats for rational laws on one key set.
221	
222	    The log-ratio is taken on integer numerators and denominators so that
223	    atoms far below float range do not underflow inside the logarithm.
224	    """
225	
226	    pi = _law(pi, "pi")
227	    p0 = _law(p0, "p0")
228	    if set(pi) != set(p0):
229	        raise ValueError("pi and p0 must share a key set")
230	    total = 0.0
231	    for key, a in pi.items():
232	        if a > 0:
233	            b = p0[key]
234	            if b == 0:
235	                raise ValueError("pi is not absolutely continuous with respect to p0")
236	            total += float(a) * (log(a.numerator) - log(a.denominator) - log(b.numerator) + log(b.denominator))
237	    return total
238	
239	
240	def beirami_radius(candidates: int) -> float:
241	    """``ln K - (K-1)/K``: the KL of a tie-free best-of-``K`` law against its base."""
242	
243	    _candidates(candidates)
244	    return log(candidates) - (candidates - 1) / candidates
245	
246	
247	def uniform_distinct_scores_kl(atoms: int, candidates: int) -> float:
248	    """``KL(pi_K || p0)`` for ``p0`` uniform on ``atoms`` records with distinct scores.
249	
250	    A Riemann sum of ``K x^{K-1} ln(K x^{K-1})`` on ``[0, 1]``; it tends to the
251	    radius as ``atoms`` grows, so the radius is the supremum over finite laws.
252	    """
253	
254	    _items(atoms)
255	    q = {Q(i): Q(1, atoms) for i in range(atoms)}
256	    return kl_divergence(max_law(q, candidates), q)
257	
258	
259	# --- the Spiral null: binomial scores ---------------------------------------------
260	
261	def binomial_score_law(items: int, p) -> dict[Q, Q]:
262	    """Law of ``S = count / items`` for ``count ~ Bin(items, p)``, keyed by the score."""
263	
264	    _items(items)
265	    p = _interior_probability(p)
266	    return {Q(j, items): Q(comb(items, j)) * p**j * (1 - p)**(items - j) for j in range(items + 1)}
267	
268	
269	def binomial_records(items: int, p) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
270	    """``(p0, score)`` on the records ``{0,1}^items`` themselves, for small ``items``."""
271	
272	    _items(items)
273	    p = _interior_probability(p)
274	    p0, score = {}, {}
275	    for bits in product("01", repeat=items):
276	        record = "".join(bits)
277	        ones = record.count("1")
278	        p0[record] = p**ones * (1 - p)**(items - ones)
279	        score[record] = Q(ones, items)
280	    return p0, score
281	
282	
283	def kl_max_law(items: int, candidates: int, p) -> float:
284	    """``KL(pi_K || p0)`` under the null, computed as the KL of the max law against one score."""
285	
286	    q = binomial_score_law(items, p)
287	    return kl_divergence(max_law(q, candidates), q)
288	
289	
290	def selection_gap(items: int, candidates: int, p) -> Q:
291	    """``gamma(items, candidates, p)`` from ``selection_inflation``."""
292	
293	    _items(items)
294	    _candidates(candidates)
295	    p = _interior_probability(p)
296	    return selection_inflation(items, candidates, p)["readout_gap"]
297	
298	
299	def gap_from_max_law(items: int, candidates: int, p) -> Q:
300	    """The same gap as ``E[S]`` under the max law minus ``p``; cross-checks ``selection_gap``."""
301

366	def _tilt(q: list[Q], scores: list[float], t: float) -> list[float]:
367	    top = max(scores)
368	    weights = [float(mass) * exp(t * (s - top)) for mass, s in zip(q, scores)]
369	    total = sum(weights)
370	    return [w / total for w in weights]

377	def kl_ball_supremum(items: int, p, radius: float) -> float:
378	    """``sup E_pi[S]`` over ``KL(pi || p0) <= radius`` under the null.
379	
380	    The supremum is attained at the exponential tilt of the score law whose
381	    KL equals the radius (bisection on the tilt parameter), or at the point
382	    mass on score 1 once ``-ln p0(1) <= radius``.
383	    """
384	
385	    _items(items)
386	    if not radius >= 0:
387	        raise ValueError("radius must be non-negative")
388	    law = binomial_score_law(items, p)
389	    keys = sorted(law)
390	    q = [law[s] for s in keys]
391	    scores = [float(s) for s in keys]
392	    if radius == 0:
393	        return float(p)
394	    if -log(float(q[-1])) <= radius + 1e-12:
395	        return 1.0
396	    lo, hi = 0.0, 1.0
397	    while _kl_float(_tilt(q, scores, hi), q) < radius:
398	        hi *= 2.0
399	    for _ in range(200):
400	        mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi)
401	        if _kl_float(_tilt(q, scores, mid), q) < radius:
402	            lo = mid
403	        else:
404	            hi = mid
405	    pi = _tilt(q, scores, lo)
406	    return sum(a * s for a, s in zip(pi, scores))

421	        raise ValueError("Simpson's rule needs an odd number of points")
422	    return float(h / 3 * (y[0] + y[-1] + 4 * y[1:-1:2].sum() + 2 * y[2:-1:2].sum()))

426	    """``E[max of candidates i.i.d. standard normals]`` by composite Simpson quadrature.
427	
428	    ``density``: ``K int x phi(x) Phi(x)^{K-1} dx``.  ``tail``: ``int_0^inf (1 - Phi^K)
429	    - int_{-inf}^0 Phi^K``.  Both on ``[-12, 12]`` with step ``1/2000``.

469	    ``sum_{s>n} C(2n-1, s-1) = 2^{2n-2}`` (half of ``2^{2n-1}``, by symmetry), while
470	    ``sum_{s>n} C(2n, s) = (4^n - C(2n, n)) / 2``; the difference is ``n C(2n, n) / 2``.

33	def _enumerate(p0, score, candidates, rule):
34	    """Independent enumeration over index tuples; the tie rule is applied literally."""
35	
36	    records = list(p0)
37	    law = {record: Q(0) for record in records}
38	    for indices in product(range(len(records)), repeat=candidates):
39	        weight = Q(1)
40	        for i in indices:
41	            weight *= p0[records[i]]
42	        if weight == 0:
43	            continue
44	        top = max(score[records[i]] for i in indices)
45	        winners = [pos for pos, i in enumerate(indices) if score[records[i]] == top]
46	        if rule == "first_index":
47	            law[records[indices[winners[0]]]] += weight
48	        else:
49	            share = weight / len(winners)
50	            for pos in winners:
51	                law[records[indices[pos]]] += share
52	    return law

from fractions import Fraction as Q

import numpy as np

def partial_sums(n):
    out, run = [], 0
    for j in range(n + 1):
        run += comb(n, j)
        out.append(run)
    return out


def M_int(n, K):
    """M_n(K) as (numerator, 2^(nK+1)) exact: M = sum_m (F - F^K), F = g/2^n."""
    g = partial_sums(n)
    T = sum(x**K for x in g[:n])
    # M = sum_{m<n} g_m/2^n - T/2^{nK} ; sum_{m<n} g_m = n 2^{n-1}
    num = n * 2**(n - 1) * 2**(n * K - n) - T  # over 2^{nK}
    return num, 2**(n * K)


def sweep(K, nmax):
    prev = None
    rows = []
    for n in range(1, nmax + 2):
        num, den = M_int(n, K)
        if prev is not None:
            pn, pd, pnn = prev
            # a_{n}^2 = M_n^2/n ; compare n_prev * M_n^2 >= (n_prev+1) * M_prev^2
            lhs = pnn * num * num * pd * pd
            rhs = (pnn + 1) * pn * pn * den * den
            ratio = Q(lhs, rhs)
            mu = 4 * pnn * (pnn + 1) * (ratio - 1)
            rho = Q(2 * pnn * (num * pd - pn * den), pn * den)
            rows.append((pnn, ratio, mu, rho))
        prev = (num, den, n)
    return rows


def gauss_moments(K):
    x = np.linspace(-12, 12, 48001)
    cdf = np.array([0.5 * erfc(-v / sqrt(2)) for v in x])
    pdf = np.exp(-0.5 * x * x) / sqrt(2 * pi)
    h = x[1] - x[0]
    dens = K * pdf * cdf ** (K - 1)
    def simpson(y):
        return float(h / 3 * (y[0] + y[-1] + 4 * y[1:-1:2].sum() + 2 * y[2:-1:2].sum()))
    m1 = simpson(x * dens)
    m3 = simpson(x ** 3 * dens)
    return m1, m3

        rhos = [r[3] for r in rows]

        m1, m3 = gauss_moments(K)

        L2 = sum(q[m] ** 2 * (w[m] if m < n else 0) for m in range(n + 1))
        L4 = sum(x ** 4 for x in q)
        gn = partial_sums(n + 1)

        S2n = sum(v * v for v in wn)

        print("identities ok at n =", n)

    Newton: ``s_K = u^K + (1-u)^K`` obeys ``s_K = s_{K-1} - w s_{K-2}``, ``s_0 = 2``, ``s_1 = 1``

def test_overlap_profile_polynomial_reproduces_every_centered_max():
    assert tie_polynomial(1) == [HALF, -1] or tie_polynomial(1) == [HALF, Q(-1)]
    assert tie_polynomial(2) == [0, 1] and tie_polynomial(3) == [0, Q(3, 2)]
    assert tie_polynomial(4) == [0, 2, -1] and tie_polynomial(5) == [0, Q(5, 2), Q(-5, 2)]
    assert tie_polynomial(6) == [0, 3, Q(-9, 2), 1]
    # 2 P_K(u(1-u)) = 1 - u^K - (1-u)^K at a few rationals u
    for k in range(1, 9):
        poly = tie_polynomial(k)
        for u in (Q(1, 3), Q(1, 7), Q(4, 5)):
            w = u * (1 - u)
            assert 2 * sum(c * w**j for j, c in enumerate(poly)) == 1 - u**k - (1 - u)**k
    for n in range(1, 16):
        profile = overlap_profile(n)
        assert len(profile) == n and profile == profile[::-1] and all(0 < w <= QUARTER for w in profile)
        q = binomial_score_law(n, HALF)
        cdf = Q(0)
        for m in range(n):
            cdf += q[Q(m, n)]
            assert profile[m] == cdf * (1 - cdf)
        for k in (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 10):

def test_pair_of_pairs_decomposition_and_second_largest_of_four():
    for n in range(1, 41):
        s1, s2 = profile_power_sums(n)
        law = max_of_two_law(n)
        assert sum(law.values()) == 1
        mad = mean_absolute_difference(law)
        # E max of four = E Y + E|Y - Y'|/2 with Y = max of two; the double sum collapses
        assert centered_max(n, 4) == s1 + mad / 2 == 2 * s1 - s2
        assert mad == 2 * (s1 - s2) and s1 == centered_max(n, 2)
        assert centered_max(n, 5) == Q(5, 2) * (s1 - s2)
        assert second_profile_increment(n) == profile_power_sums(n + 1)[1] - s2
        assert quadruple_increment(n) == centered_max_increment(n, 4) == centered_max(n + 1, 4) - centered_max(n, 4)
    for n in (1, 2, 3):
        s1, s2 = profile_power_sums(n)
        assert order_statistic_mean_by_enumeration(n, 4, 3) == 3 * s2
        assert order_statistic_mean_by_enumeration(n, 4, 2) == -3 * s2
        assert order_statistic_mean_by_enumeration(n, 4, 4) == centered_max(n, 4)
        assert order_statistic_mean_by_enumeration(n, 3, 2) == 0 and order_statistic_mean_by_enumeration(n, 2, 2) == s1
    local = local_sums(1)
    assert local == {"L1": HALF, "L2": Q(1, 16), "L4": Q(1, 8)}
    assert profile_power_sums(1) == (QUARTER, Q(1, 16)) and profile_power_sums(2) == (Q(3, 8), Q(9, 128))
    assert local_sums(3)["L4"] == Q(1 + 27 + 27 + 1, 4**3)


def test_tie_count_law_and_the_crude_tie_bound_witness():
    for n, k in ((1, 2), (2, 2), (2, 3), (3, 3), (2, 4), (3, 4), (1, 5)):
        law = tie_count_law(n, k)
        total = Q(0)
        q = binomial_score_law(n, HALF)
        masses = [q[Q(j, n)] for j in range(n + 1)]
        brute = {j: Q(0) for j in range(1, k + 1)}
        for counts in product(range(n + 1), repeat=k):
            weight = Q(1)
            for c in counts:
                weight *= masses[c]
            brute[counts.count(max(counts))] += weight
        assert law == brute and sum(law.values()) == 1
        assert sum(p for j, p in law.items() if j >= 2) == tie_mass(n, k)
        assert sum(Q(1, 2**j) * p for j, p in law.items()) == tie_count_moment(n, k)
    for n in range(1, 31):
        cubes = sum(Q(comb(n, m), 2**n)**3 for m in range(n + 1))
        assert crude_tie_bound_deficit(n, 2) == 0
        assert crude_tie_bound_deficit(n, 3) == -Q(n, 2) * cubes < 0
        assert crude_tie_bound_deficit(n, 4) < 0 and crude_tie_bound_deficit(n, 7) < 0
        # P(N >= 2) for K = 3 is (3/2) sum q^2 - (1/2) sum q^3 by the symmetry m -> n - m
        squares = sum(Q(comb(n, m), 2**n)**2 for m in range(n + 1))
        assert tie_mass(n, 3) == Q(3, 2) * squares - cubes / 2
    assert crude_tie_bound_deficit(1, 3) == -Q(1, 8) and crude_tie_bound_deficit(2, 4) == -Q(17, 64)


def test_rational_step_ratio_exists_for_pairs_and_triples_only():
    for k in (2, 3):
        assert rational_step_ratio_rank(lambda n, k=k: centered_max(n, k), 1)["exists"]
    for degree in (1, 2, 3, 4, 6):
        report = rational_step_ratio_rank(lambda n: centered_max(n, 4), degree)
        assert not report["exists"] and report["rank"] == report["columns"] == 2 * (degree + 1)
    assert not rational_step_ratio_rank(lambda n: mean_absolute_difference(max_of_two_law(n)), 4)["exists"]
    # positive control: a hypergeometric sequence passes at degree 1
    assert rational_step_ratio_rank(lambda n: Q(comb(2 * n, n), 4**n), 1)["exists"]


def test_quadruple_recurrence_is_found_and_holds_far_beyond_the_fit():
    assert quadruple_numerator(1) == 2**5 * Q(7, 16) and quadruple_numerator(2) == 2**9 * Q(87, 128)
    rec = quadruple_recurrence(verify_items=200)
    assert rec["order"] == 4 and rec["degree"] == 8 and rec["nullity"] == 1 and rec["verified"]
    assert rec["characteristic_monic"] == [2048, 1280, 72, -26, 1]
    assert all(rec["characteristic_roots"].values())
    assert all(v == 0 for v in rec["lower_order_nullity"].values())
    coefficients = rec["coefficients"]
    for n in (201, 250, 333):
        assert sum(sum(poly[d] * n**d for d in range(9)) * quadruple_numerator(n + i) for i, poly in enumerate(coefficients)) == 0
    # the guesser on a known hypergeometric sequence: C(2n, n) obeys (n+1) a_{n+1} - (4n+2) a_n = 0
    basis = guess_recurrence(lambda n: Q(comb(2 * n, n)), 1, 1, 8)
    assert len(basis) == 1
    (p0, p1), = basis
    assert p0[1] / p1[1] == -4 and p0[0] / p1[1] == -2 and p1[0] / p1[1] == 1


def test_gaussian_third_moment_margin_limit():
    assert abs(gaussian_max_moment(2, 1) - gaussian_max_expectation(2)) <= 1e-12
    assert abs(gaussian_max_moment(1, 2) - 1) <= 1e-9 and abs(gaussian_max_moment(1, 3)) <= 1e-9
    assert abs(gaussian_max_moment(2, 3) - 2.5 / sqrt(pi)) <= 1e-9
    assert abs(gaussian_max_moment(3, 3) - 15 / (4 * sqrt(pi))) <= 1e-9
    assert abs(asymptotic_margin(2)) <= 1e-9 and abs(asymptotic_margin(3)) <= 1e-9
    values = [asymptotic_margin(k) for k in range(4, 31)]
    assert all(v > 0 for v in values) and values == sorted(values)
    assert abs(asymptotic_margin(4) - 0.0205606) < 2e-7 and abs(asymptotic_margin(10) - 0.159103) < 2e-6
    assert abs(asymptotic_normalized_margin(4) - 1.08224) < 2e-5
    # the exact sweep's n(rho_n - 1) approaches c(K) from above at K = 4
    excess = [n * (increment_ratio(n, 4) - 1) for n in (50, 100, 200)]
    assert all(float(e) > asymptotic_margin(4) for e in excess)
    assert all(abs(float(e) - asymptotic_margin(4)) < 0.03 / n for e, n in zip(excess, (50, 100, 200)))


def test_wide_sweep_agrees_with_the_rational_sweep_on_small_ranges():
    wide = wide_monotonicity_sweep((2, 3, 4, 7, 10), 60)
    for k in (2, 3, 4, 7, 10):
        row, reference = wide[f"K={k}"], monotonicity_sweep(k, 60)
        assert row["monotone"] and row["first_failure"] is None and row["rho_at_least_one"]
        assert row["min_margin_at"] == reference["min_margin_at"] and row["min_rho_at"] == reference["min_rho_at"]
        assert abs(row["min_margin"] - reference["min_margin"]) <= 1e-9 * reference["min_margin"]
        assert abs(row["min_rho"] - reference["min_rho"]) <= 1e-12
        assert abs(row["margins"]["n=60"] - float(4 * 60 * 61 * (scaled_gap_squared(61, k) / scaled_gap_squared(60, k) - 1))) <= 1e-9
    assert wide["K=2"]["min_margin"] == 1.0 and wide["K=3"]["min_margin"] == 1.0
    assert wide["K=4"]["richardson_minus_gaussian"] is not None and abs(wide["K=4"]["richardson_minus_gaussian"]) < 1e-4
    huge = wide_monotonicity_sweep((300,), 12)
    assert huge["K=300"]["monotone"] and huge["K=300"]["min_margin"] > 1

*\(K\ge4\), version 0.3: the overlap profile.* Write \(w_m=F_n(m)(1-F_n(m))=P(X\le m<X')\), \(m<n\). Since \(F_n(n-1-m)=1-F_n(m)\), \(M_n(K)=\sum_{m<n}[F_n(m)-F_n(m)^K]=\sum_mP_K(w_m)\) with \(2P_K(u(1-u))=1-u^K-(1-u)^K\) (Newton: \(P_2=w\), \(P_3=\tfrac32w\), \(P_4=2w-w^2\), \(P_5=\tfrac52(w-w^2)\); `tie_polynomial`, checked against `centered_max`, \(n\le40\), \(K\le12\)). With \(S_j=\sum_mw_m^j\): \(M_n(2)=S_1\), \(M_n(4)=2S_1-S_2\), and the pair-of-pairs step of R1, \(M_n(4)=M_n(2)+\tfrac12\mathbb E|Y-Y'|\) with \(Y\) the max of two, has \(\mathbb E|Y-Y'|=2\sum_mF_Y(1-F_Y)=2(S_1-S_2)\): the double sum collapses (identity, \(n\le60\)); also \(\mathbb EY_{(3:4)}=3S_2\) (enumerated, \(n\le4\)). The step \(n\to n+1\) replaces \(F_n\) by the midpoints of \((0,F_n,1)\), so \(v_m=\tfrac12(w_{m-1}+w_m)+\tfrac14q_m^2\), and with the local sums \(L_1=\sum_mq_m^2\), \(L_2=\sum_mq_m^2w_m\), \(L_4=\sum_mq_m^4\): \(S_2^{(n+1)}-S_2^{(n)}=\tfrac14(6L_2-L_1)+\tfrac5{16}L_4\) and \(M_{n+1}(4)-M_n(4)=\tfrac34L_1-\tfrac32L_2-\tfrac5{16}L_4\) (identities, \(n\le60\)). Hence \(\rho_n(4)\ge1\iff S_2\ge n[3L_2+\tfrac58L_4-\tfrac12L_1]\), the \(K=4\) analogue of de Moivre's \(S_1=\tfrac n2L_1\) — but an inequality, not an identity.
*Why R1 fails.* \(S_2=\mathbb EY_{(3:4)}/3\) is not a local sum, \(L_4=\sum_m\binom nm^4/16^n\) is a Franel-type sum (numerators 1, 2, 18, 164, 1810), and the step ratio \(M_{n+1}(4)/M_n(4)\) is not a rational function of \(n\): the linear system \(p(n)=r_ns(n)\) has full column rank for every degree \(\le6\) (exact; at degree 1 the system is solved by \((2n+1)/(2n)\) for \(K=2,3\)), and likewise for \(\mathbb E|Y-Y'|\). What exists instead: \(u_n=2^{4n+1}M_n(4)\) satisfies an order-4 recurrence with degree-8 integer coefficients (nullity one on 53 terms, verified for \(n\le300\); none of order \(\le3\) through degree 12), characteristic polynomial \((x-16)^2(x+2)(x+4)\) — the double root carries \(16^n\sqrt n\), the roots \(-2,-4\) are exponentially small parity terms. So the \(K=2\) telescoping has no analogue; a proof would be an order-4 interval induction on that recurrence, not attempted. \(K=5\) and \(K=8\) inherit the status of \(K=4\).
*Why R2 fails.* \(\tfrac12-2^{-j}\ge\tfrac14\) for \(j\ge2\) gives \(M_{n+1}-M_n\ge P(N_n\ge2)/4\), so \(nP(N_n\ge2)\ge2M_n\) would prove \(\rho_n\ge1\); \(P(N\ge2)=\sum_m[F(m)^K-F(m-1)^K-Kq_mF(m-1)^{K-1}]\) and \(P(N=j)=\sum_m\binom Kjq_m^jF(m-1)^{K-j}\) (exact, enumerated). The bound is an identity for \(K=2\) (\(N\le2\)) and fails at every \(n\) for \(K=3\), where \(\rho_n=1\): by \(m\to n-m\), \(P(N\ge2)=\tfrac32\sum q_m^2-\tfrac12\sum q_m^3\), so \(nP(N\ge2)-2M_n(3)=-\tfrac n2\sum_mq_m^3<0\) exactly (\(-\tfrac18,-\tfrac5{32},-\tfrac{21}{128},\dots\); \(n\le60\)); it fails for \(K=4\) too (\(-\tfrac18,-\tfrac{17}{64},\dots\)). The lost mass is the extra \(\tfrac18\) on triple ties, and restoring the weights \(\tfrac12-2^{-j}\) returns the increment identity itself.
*The asymptotic margin.* Continuity-corrected Edgeworth at \(p=\tfrac12\): \(F_n(m)=\Phi(z)+\varphi(z)(z^3-z)/(12n)+O(n^{-2})\), \(z=(2m+1-n)/\sqrt n\) (lattice plus kurtosis terms); the midpoint sum of \(\varphi_K\circ\Phi\), \(2\varphi_K(u)=1-u^K-(1-u)^K\), has exponentially small error (Poisson), so \(M_n(K)=\tfrac{\sqrt n}2\mathbb E[M_K]-\mathbb E[M_K^3-M_K]/(24\sqrt n)+O(n^{-3/2})\), \(\mu_n\to\mu_\infty(K)=\tfrac23\mathbb E[M_K^3-M_K]/\mathbb E[M_K]\) and \(n(\rho_n-1)\to c(K)=(\mu_\infty-1)/4=(\mathbb E[M_K^3]-\tfrac52\mathbb E[M_K])/(6\mathbb E[M_K])\). Smallest margin anywhere: \(\mu_{400}(4)=1.08262\) (\(\rho_{400}(4)=1.0000516\)), above its limit 1.08224; at \(n=400\) the margin exceeds \(\mu_\infty(K)\) for every \(K\le100\) (approach from above: \(n(\rho_n-1)-c(K)\approx0.028/n\) at \(K=4\)). The minimum over \(n\) sits at \(n=400\) for \(K=4..19\) (and for 28–36, 62–70) and near \(n\approx\log_2K\) otherwise, where a wobble dips below \(\mu_\infty\) but never below 2: \(K=20\): 2.207 at \(n=4\); 50: 2.621 at 5; 100: 2.826 at 6; 200: 2.956 at 7; 500: 4.368 at 8; 1000: 4.615 at 9; \(10^4\): 3.965 at 13. Status: theorem for \(K=2,3\); for every \(K\ge4\) a finite verified example on these ranges plus a cited asymptotic with positive limit margin.
